Square root of two is irrational: either a geometric descent or the usual even-numerator/even-denominator contradiction rules out a reduced rational fraction. The rational set below square root of two has upper bounds but no least rational upper bound, motivating a gap-free real continuum.

unit_reviews.reverse_sample: A real is represented by a nonempty proper initial segment of the rationals with no greatest element. Inclusion orders these cuts. For any nonempty upper-bounded set of cuts, its union is itself a cut, contains every member of the family, and lies inside every other upper bound, so it is the least upper bound. Rational p embeds as the cut of rationals below p; arithmetic is then defined on cuts.

unit_reviews.checks: Compared all eleven translated paragraph blocks, including the conceptual value of completeness and Dedekind construction, three reservations about rigor and metaphysical identity, alternative ordered-pair constructions and the Benacerraf citation, the nonidentity of natural and constructed integer zero, the weaker treat-as/embed conclusion, the closing qualification, and all inactive explanatory comments. unit_reviews.reverse_sample: The constructions establish coherent complete ordered fields and put analysis on a rigorous basis, but set encodings alone need not add rigor or reveal what numbers metaphysically are. Alternative pair encodings yield different set objects, and constructed integer zero is not literally natural zero. Naive set theory therefore lets us treat numbers as sets and embed their theories, while the philosophical significance needs further argument.
